Native Persistence

1. What is Native Persistence?
  • Native Persistence stores data on disk in addition to RAM, allowing the cluster to survive full restarts without data loss;
  • Data is written to disk in the same page format used in memory — no serialization overhead;
  • RAM acts as a caching layer over disk: hot data is in memory, cold data is on disk;
  • When the data set exceeds available RAM, Ignite transparently reads pages from disk;
2. Enabling Native Persistence
  • DataStorageConfiguration storageCfg = new DataStorageConfiguration();

DataRegionConfiguration regionCfg = new DataRegionConfiguration();
regionCfg.setName("persistentRegion");
regionCfg.setPersistenceEnabled(true);           // enable persistence
regionCfg.setInitialSize(100L * 1024 * 1024);    // 100 MB initial memory
regionCfg.setMaxSize(500L * 1024 * 1024);        // 500 MB max memory

storageCfg.setDefaultDataRegionConfiguration(regionCfg);

IgniteConfiguration cfg = new IgniteConfiguration();
cfg.setDataStorageConfiguration(storageCfg);
  • After enabling persistence, you must activate the cluster before using caches: 
    ignite.cluster().state(ClusterState.ACTIVE);
3. How it Works Under the Hood
  • Ignite uses a Write-Ahead Log (WAL) to ensure durability:
    1. Every write is first recorded in the WAL;
    2. The in-memory page is updated;
    3. Dirty pages are periodically flushed to the main storage (partition files) during checkpointing;
  • On restart, Ignite reads the partition files and replays the WAL to recover any changes made after the last checkpoint;
4. WAL Modes
ModeDurabilityPerformance
FSYNC Highest — every WAL record is fsync'd to disk Slowest
LOG_ONLY (default) High — writes go to OS page cache; lost only on OS crash Fast
BACKGROUND Medium — WAL fsync'd in the background at intervals Faster
NONE None — WAL is disabled; data may be lost on crash Fastest 
storageCfg.setWalMode(WALMode.LOG_ONLY);
5. Checkpointing
  • Checkpointing flushes dirty memory pages to disk;
  • After a checkpoint, the WAL records before the checkpoint are no longer needed for recovery;
  • Checkpoint frequency: 
    storageCfg.setCheckpointFrequency(180_000); // every 3 minutes (default)
6. Data Regions
  • You can define multiple data regions with different settings (persistent vs. in-memory, different sizes): 
    // Persistent region for important data
DataRegionConfiguration persistentRegion = new DataRegionConfiguration();
persistentRegion.setName("persistent");
persistentRegion.setPersistenceEnabled(true);
persistentRegion.setMaxSize(1L * 1024 * 1024 * 1024); // 1 GB

// In-memory region for temporary data
DataRegionConfiguration volatileRegion = new DataRegionConfiguration();
volatileRegion.setName("volatile");
volatileRegion.setPersistenceEnabled(false);
volatileRegion.setMaxSize(256L * 1024 * 1024); // 256 MB

storageCfg.setDataRegionConfigurations(persistentRegion, volatileRegion);

// Assign a cache to a region
CacheConfiguration cacheCfg = new CacheConfiguration("tempCache");
cacheCfg.setDataRegionName("volatile");
